messages:
anika: Quick design check: proposing a "tenant-tier fallback partitioner" (working name). Goal: stop one noisy tenant from draining global fallback and creating oscillation. Unlike slabs, this uses per-tier lockers and a soft "warmness" score to bias reclaim. Short sketch below.

anika: Problem: current global fallback pool is a free-for-all under spikes. We see churn and repeated model rehydrates that spike p95 for stable tenants. Partitioner idea: partition pool by tier lockers but allow controlled transfers under cost pressure.

diego: How is locker different from slab? sounds similar but name implies lock semantics.

anika: Locker = capacity bucket with soft reservations and a small transfer window. Reservations are lease-like; lockers maintain a "warmness" score (0..1) based on KV residency, recent QPS, and last-eviction-time. Lower warmness -> higher reclaim priority.

olga: Important: we must avoid thrashing where tenant loses locker -> rehydrate -> loses again. Propose tracking "eviction_debt" per tenant and disabling re-assign for N minutes when debt > threshold.

anika: Good. Also plan to emit a preempt_hint token to runtime: {locker_id, preemptible_until, rehydrate_path}. Runtime can reply with estimated rehydrate_ms and current warmness. If rehydrate_ms > grace_window, partitioner will back off.

sam: Ops: rollout phases like usual but include a chaos test step to intentionally spike a mid-tier tenant. Phases:
- dry-run: decisions logged only
- advisory: runtime honors hints but still follows existing fallback if conflicts
- enforce: partitioner enforces lockers and transfers are allowed only under cost_pressure high flag

anika: proto-config (pseudo-yaml):

```
partitioner:
  fallback_pool_mb: 1048576
  tiers:
    - name: dev
      locker_pct: 5
      min_reserve_mb: 1024
    - name: team
      locker_pct: 45
      min_reserve_mb: 65536
    - name: business
      locker_pct: 50
      min_reserve_mb: 262144
  soft_lease_secs: 240
  grace_window_ms: 45000
  transfer_window_secs: 120
  eviction_debt_threshold: 3
  cost_pressure_map:
    low: 1.0
    normal: 0.85
    high: 0.6
```

anika: Notes: locker_pct sums ~=100. min_reserve sets a floor so tiny tenants still get minimal capability. transfer_window is how long a locker can accept borrowed capacity before returning it.

diego: Telemetry: add metrics `locker_warmness`, `eviction_debt`, `locker_churn_rate`, `rehydrate_ms_estimate`, and `preempt_hints_accepted`. Dashboards per-tenant and per-tier. Alert if any priority-0 tenant p95 increases >8% during advisory.

olga: Runtime contract: implement `preempt_hint(token)` callback that returns {accepted:bool, est_rehydrate_ms:int}. If accepted=false, partitioner should postpone reclaim for soft_lease_secs. Also need an API to request a KV snapshot URL (rehydrate_path) if runtime supports fast rehydrate.

sam: deploy-bot: scheduling dry-run simulation: 2026-04-10T02:00:00Z. Will post summary to #eng-runtime.

deploy-bot: simulation_scheduled thread=1810105000 mode=dry-run start_ts=1810110000

anika: Cost integration: partitioner will listen to `cost_pressure` signal (enum low/normal/high). On high, reduce dev/team lockers proportionally to protect business tier. Also, during high cost we increase aggressiveness of transfer_window expirations.

diego: Implementation note: locker accounting should convert model variants to VRAM-equivalent units. Add `vram_factor` to model catalog and charge lockers in vram_equiv.

olga: Tests:
- single tenant spike vs other steady tenants -> ensure steady tenants p50 unchanged and no >5% p95 bump
- repeated reclaim cycles -> ensure eviction_debt prevents thrash
- cost_pressure high -> verify automatic shrink of non-critical lockers
- rehydrate_path respected -> rehydrate_ms stays < grace_window for >95% of reclaims

anika: Owners: Diego = partitioner service + telemetry, Olga = runtime preempt hook + rehydrate API, Sam = canary plan + ops playbook. I'll write RFC follow-up with these decisions and config.

sam: Action items:
- diego: dry-run branch + dashboard mock by next Tue
- olga: runtime hook spec + mock acceptance logic by EOW
- anika: RFC follow-up + test matrix

diego: LGTM.

olga: lgtm.
